evidence.claim: a versioned scoring model produces a ScoreRun with per-rule contributions, reproducible for identical inputs and clamped to declared bounds
the model version is persisted with a fingerprint, so a historical score names the model that produced it

limitations: lead scoring only: no account scoring exists, and the canonical job names both

the model is a versioned deterministic rule set, not a learned model — there is no label set, no baseline, no holdout, no calibration and no drift or leakage monitoring, all of which the canonical job's flow requires
the score is explainable per rule, which is not the canonical 'sources, freshness, assumptions and confidence' surface
no identity verifier ships, so scope-restricted reads of a score cannot be proven end to end

evidence.claim: a checked-in manifest becomes a migrated, registered, runnable module with no page code written
the generated module is reachable over the real HTTP API and the SDK, and appears in /api/schema
a generated-to-generated many-to-one relation is enforced by a foreign key, validated at runtime and survives restart
the generated Admin lists, creates, opens and edits the record, producing audit and events

limitations: layout is not configurable: field order comes from the manifest and there is no section, responsive or component layer (the matrix's own JTBD-DC-03 is 'not supported')
the canonical acceptance criterion requires Accordo to show sources, freshness, assumptions and confidence before the change is made; no such surface exists anywhere in the framework
migrations are versioned and forward-only, so the canonical clause that every high-impact action be revocable or compensable is unmet
no identity verifier ships, so 'a user with valid scope' is an assertion a deployment supplies rather than something this repository can prove
no retention or archival behaviour exists, which the canonical non-functional requirement names

evidence.claim: a deterministic policy parks the deal in Approval Pending and only actor.type === 'user' may decide, with trace and audit recorded
the approval decision is reachable and refused over the public HTTP boundary on the same rule
a discount above the versioned policy threshold requires a human decision before the quote version is approved

limitations: nothing is routed: the record parks for any human holding the permission, and there is no approval matrix, no named approver and no ownership assignment — the canonical outcome 'assign each record once, to the correct owner' is not met

no SLA is measured end to end: a durable job store and scheduled timers now exist (spine.durable_job_store.implemented=implemented), but nothing measures an SLA against them, no worker service runs them for you (spine.managed_jobs_service.implemented=absent), and a timer opens an ask rather than escalating one
the canonical acceptance criterion requires sources, freshness and confidence to be shown before the decision; the approval surface shows the record and the policy outcome only
no identity verifier ships, so the human who decided is only as trustworthy as the adapter a deployment supplies

evidence.claim: a quote is priced on the server from a price book, frozen into an immutable Quote Version, and a discount is decided by a versioned policy with human approval
the quote version snapshot is never rewritten by later movement in the catalog it was priced from
the quote and its versions render in the Admin with server-computed totals

limitations: no document is produced: the canonical job asks for a quote *and its documents*, and Accordo produces an immutable Quote Version record with no rendering, template or file artefact
the external catalog is a fixture provider behind the real provider contract; no real Stripe/Zuora/ERP catalog is validated
the canonical acceptance criterion requires sources, freshness and confidence before the decision; the quote surface shows priced lines and a policy outcome only
no identity verifier ships, so the approver's identity is supplied by the deployment

evidence.claim: an approved quote version becomes an envelope, verified provider events drive signer state, and a signed Order snapshot is built immutably from it
the envelope state machine has an explicit transition table, terminal states never regress, and a replayed webhook creates no second effect

limitations: the signature provider is a deterministic fixture behind the real provider contract; no commercial e-sign vendor is validated, and no human-approved credential is exercised
the webhook signing key is test-only and the signed-artifact hash is provider-reported rather than independently recomputed
no redline, no counterparty negotiation and no legal review step exists, which the canonical flow places before signature
no identity verifier ships, so the signer is an assertion the provider makes
